correctness.rationale: Checked RESULT.md lines 27–58 from the literal corner-overlap definition, including self-pairs. The observed corner sets A,B are disjoint. A two-square equality requires the prefix matrix center in B and the suffix matrix center in A; the common square is a unique component label. For sizes a,b this yields abq² disjoint complete bipartite components with side sizes bq⁴ and aq⁴, plus ab(q−a−b)q⁶ isolated vertices. A maximum takes the whole larger side (either entire side on a tie), giving ab(q−min(a,b))q⁶. With a≥b, equality in a≤q−b is necessary, and comparing the integers next to q/3 gives the unique smaller size floor((q+1)/3). This forces both large-alphabet orientations and the stated labeled count. For q=2, the four K(16,16) per orientation give sixteen choices each; only the two constant-side choices per orientation are unrestricted diagonal lifts. Inspected VERIFICATION.md and all three scripts without executing them. Their finite scope is supplementary; the exact graph argument supplies the universal upper bound and equality cases.
